title: Chromatic index of an even regular graph with one edge subdivided
statement: Let $G$ be a $k$-regular simple graph, with $k \ge 2$, on a finite vertex set whose cardinality is even, and let $uv$ be an edge of $G$. Form the graph $G'$ by subdividing the edge $uv$: delete it and join its ends $u$ and $v$ by a path of length two through a single new vertex. Then the chromatic number of the line graph of $G'$ — equivalently, the edge chromatic number $\chi'(G')$ — equals $\Delta(G') + 1$, where $\Delta(G')$ is the maximum degree of $G'$.
hypotheses_covered: $G$ is a simple graph on a finite vertex set
the number of vertices is even
